brief: The fact that changes tonight: Your log stamps every night since 28 October as Meso 3 (week 5 on 28 October, week 9 on 25 November), while the calendar has been Meso 3b since 28 October and the lighter week since 25 November. The app stamps Meso 3 on those dates only when the phase is locked by hand in its phase menu, so your phone is locked to Meso 3. Under that lock the app sets aside any review written for a different kind of phase, and the calendar makes this week's reviews lighter-week reviews, so this review's numbers do not reach your card; the app's own build numbers run instead, at full sets. The same will happen to every review from here on while the lock stays, because 2 to 8 December is assessment and prep starts 9 December, and neither is a build phase; the app's card tells you this too and says that setting the phase back to Automatic lets the review through. The lock is yours and I cannot change it from here. It also corrects what I wrote yesterday: Legs B on 25 November was heavy because the app gave you its build card, not because you skipped a lighter one, and my sentences saying the app holds every card to two sets this week are not true on your phone. What your phone shows tonight for Push A, from the app's own rules (I did not set these): Smith incline 165 for 8, then 180 for 8, 8, 8; chest press 165 for 10, three sets; low-to-high crossover 17.5 for 12, three sets; lateral raise 17.5 for 15, four sets; chest dip bodyweight 12, three sets; neck flexion 10 lb for 15, two sets. Two of those are bigger jumps than I would give: the crossover goes from 12.5 (your best, 15 reps on all three on 15 November) straight to 17.5, and neck flexion has never been done and starts at 10. This review's numbers, which show only with the phase on Automatic: two sets each of Smith incline 180 for 7, chest press 165 for 10, crossover 12.5 for 15, lateral raise 17.5 for 13, chest dip bodyweight 12, and one set of neck flexion at 5 lb for 15. Every one of those is a weight and rep count you have already done at this gym except neck flexion, which is new and where the 5 lb is my choice, not a measured number. Those asks changed from yesterday's in one way: no rep or weight records in a week the calendar calls lighter (yesterday asked 13.75 on the crossover, 14 on laterals and 13 on dips). Nothing new has been logged since 25 November; if you trained on 26 November and the log is late, tomorrow's review reads it. No program change today: version 18 (26 November) stands, with the single-leg dumbbell calf raise after the calf press on Legs B. Side delts, and whether triceps get isolation work on Push A, are decided on 2 December. Dates: lighter week ends 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December, show 1 March, 94 days away. What I still need: a morning bodyweight (nothing logged since 23 August, 207 lb, 96 days; the Bodyweight button on the workout screen), and your division.

side-delts.why: Raised on 18 November (version 14). Side delts decide how wide the shoulders look on stage; they had the smallest share of any scored muscle (6 direct sets, 8 counted, against 15.5 for rear delts), so lateral raises went to four sets on each push day: 8 direct, 10 counted with half credit from the shoulder press, the bottom of the 10 to 20 range. First four-set night, 23 November on Push B: 17.5 for 13, 13, 13 and the fourth set was not done, and you asked why four sets for a small muscle. The honest count: the 6.3 a week done is an average over weeks that include rest days and a partial week (the week of 17 to 22 November had no push night) and mostly predate the four-set cards, so it does not prove the fourth set is the problem; there has been exactly one four-set night and three of four sets were done. Direct sets are now 8 against the rear delts' 7; on the counted number it is 10 against 12.5. 15 November on Push A was 17.5 for 12, 12, 12 (three sets, before the fourth existed). The weight is right (17.5, up from 15). The decision between a third lateral day and a second side-delt lift stays with the review of 2 December: the calendar's lighter week (25 November to 1 December) is a poor week to add a day, and adding a day now would walk back the 14 November removal of the Pull A cable lateral raise (version 12) inside the 14-day guard. Honest limit on the date: this review's cards are two sets this week, and with your phase locked to Meso 3 the app's own card asks four sets of 17.5 for 15; whatever Push A logs this week is read on 2 December, so this week's Push A may or may not show whether a fourth lateral set at 17.5 works. What 2 December adds is calendar, not new evidence: it is the first review after the lighter week ends (1 December is its last day), and the decision (a third lateral day or a second side-delt lift) is made then on the 23 November night and whatever Push A shows. Until then side delts stay at 8 direct, 10 counted, the floor of their range. Counted with half credit for helper muscles: 10 planned a week, of which 8 are direct sets; 6.3 a week done on average over the last four weeks.

Both rows are going up: seated row 112.5 for 10 on all four on 16 November, chest-supported row 60 for 10 on all four on 24 November (9 on 13 November). Hold. prep.plan: Twelve days come before prep (from 27 November). The build block ended on 24 November. The calendar calls 25 November to 1 December a lighter week; this review's cards are two sets of proven weights, but your phone's phase is locked to Meso 3, so the app runs its own build numbers instead (see the block). While that lock stays, assessment and prep reviews are set aside the same way, so this plan reaches your card only with the phase on Automatic. The week of 2 December is assessment: each main lift is run at its current weight for its best reps, and the starting bodyweight is set. Prep starts on 9 December and runs just under 12 weeks. Weeks 1 to 4 (9 December to 5 January): the same lifts and weights as now, with the sets as they stand after the side-delt decision (2 December review) and the second calf lift added on 26 November; in prep, holding reps at the same weight while bodyweight comes down is the win. Weeks 5 to 8 (6 January to 2 February): the weights stay, and if recovery slips, sets come off what the stage scores least (rear delts, forearms, traps, the hip machines) before anything comes off side delts, back, chest, arms, quads or calves. Weeks 9 to 11 (3 to 23 February): the same, no new lifts, no set taken to a grinding rep. The final week (24 February to 1 March, show day): about half the sets, with the last hard leg session early in the week. Fat loss is paced at about half a percent to one percent of bodyweight a week, which at your last logged 207 lb is about 1 to 2 lb a week. It is checked by the weekly average of morning weigh-ins: less than half a percent for two weeks running means food or daily walking has to change; more than one percent with reps dropping means it is too fast. From 9 December to the show is just under 12 weeks, so at that pace the most that can come off is roughly 12 to 23 lb from 207. Whether that is enough is not something I can tell: the last weigh-in in the log is 23 August, and there are no photos and no division. If more than that has to come off, the only slack is the 12 days before 9 December, which is why the weigh-in matters now and not in December. The prep phase in the calendar is a placeholder that detailed programming replaces at assessment, so this plan is a default, not a decision. What it protects, in order, once real data arrives: side delts, upper chest (Push A), back, arms, quads, calves; the deadlift and RDL are climbing 5 to 10 lb a visit now (deadlift 250 for 5 on 16 November) and in a deficit they hold their weight rather than climb. If no bodyweight arrives by 2 December, I will start prep on 9 December from 207 lb (23 August) and say so. Assessment (2 to 8 December) reads each main lift at its current weight for its best reps; if two of them come in under their reps of 15 to 25 November, prep starts with sets coming off the least-scored muscles at once, not in week 5. In prep, a cut in sets is triggered by any week where two or more main lifts fall below their previous reps or where a session ends with its late slots skipped.
